description: Cross-language plugin registry for AI/orchestration applications — folder-based discovery, TOML manifests, pluggy-based Python binding, single contract across Python, TypeScript, and Go.
rules: Install with: pip install dagstack-plugin-system (Python, pypi.org) / npm install @dagstack/plugin-system (TypeScript, npmjs.org, roadmap) / go get go.dagstack.dev/plugin-system (Go vanity, roadmap).
Use discover(path) to scan a folder for plugins — it walks directories for dagstack.toml manifest files and returns a PluginRegistry with all validated plugins.
Every plugin directory must contain a dagstack.toml with at least: [plugin] name, kind, runtime, core_version — discovery skips folders missing the manifest.
Plugin kinds are namespaced identifiers like llm, vector_store, chunker, pipeline, tool, orchestrator — kinds register their hookspecs, plugins declare the kind they implement.
Runtime values are in_process (same language, direct call), mcp_stdio (subprocess over stdio), or mcp_http (remote HTTP service) — the same plugin manifest can declare support for multiple runtimes.
Call PluginRegistry.setup_all() once after discover() and before any hook invocation — it triggers per-plugin setup() and validates cross-plugin dependencies via topo_sort.
Retrieve plugin instances via registry.get(kind, name) — the returned proxy applies dispatch rules from the kind's hookspec, injects resources, and runs contract checks.

execution_model declares hook-execution style (sync | async | thread_cpu_bound | process_cpu_bound) in the plugin manifest — this is NOT the dispatch class. Dispatch classes (singleton, broadcast_collect, broadcast_notify, chain, capability) are declared in the kind's hookspec, not in plugin manifest.

Resources are injected via PluginContext.resources at setup() — do not create HTTP clients, DB connections, or file handles inside the plugin constructor. Standard resources: clock, rng, http_client, blob_store, tmpdir. Custom resources registered via ResourceRegistry.register() in application startup.

Unit of Work for long-running plugins is declared in manifest [plugin.unit_of_work]: partition_key (sharding), idempotency_mode (input_hash | output_hash | none), checkpointable (supports ctx.checkpoint for resume after crash), content_hash (fields used to compute idempotency key).

Horizontal middleware (governance, quota, observability) uses chain dispatch with priority >= 1000 — this range is reserved. Business plugins must keep priority < 1000. Governance middleware wraps hooks via [plugin.chain_wrap] kinds and hooks, accessing ctx.metadata for tenant_id, actor, trace_context.

Override active singleton plugin via DAGSTACK_ACTIVE_<KIND>=<plugin_name> environment variable, without editing manifests. Routing policies set via registry.set_routing_policy(kind, policy_fn) for per-tenant/blue-green/canary selection at runtime.

Hook invocation has five dispatch classes: Singleton (one plugin), Broadcast-Collect (all plugins, aggregate results), Broadcast-Notify (all plugins, fire-and-forget), Chain (sequential with STOP_CHAIN short-circuit), Dispatch-by-capability (first plugin matching capabilities).
Use BroadcastCollectDispatcher when every registered plugin must process the call and contribute a result (for example producing embeddings, gathering search results).
Use ChainDispatcher with MIDDLEWARE_PRIORITY_THRESHOLD for middleware-style pipelines — priority above threshold runs before core plugins, below runs after.
Use CapabilityDispatcher when only one plugin is allowed to match a request based on declared capabilities — raises NoCapabilityMatch if no plugin matches.
Declare resource dependencies in manifest resources.required — the registry injects them via ResourceContainer using inject_resources, matching by Protocol (Clock, Rng, BlobStore, HttpClient).
Use FrozenClock and DeterministicRng from STANDARD_RESOURCES in tests to get reproducible time and randomness — replace SystemClock and RandomRng at the container level.

Plugins must honour the eight runtime invariants: no ambient state, serialisable boundaries, declared resources, explicit sync/async, partition keys, abstract ProgressSink/CheckpointStore, content-hash idempotency, determinism boundary.

Run contract tests via run_contract_suite(plugin) — it executes assert_manifest_valid, assert_lifecycle_clean, assert_no_ambient_state, assert_json_serializable_boundaries, assert_deterministic against the plugin.

Errors subclass PluginRegistryError: ManifestInvalid (schema violation), AmbiguousPlugin (two plugins same kind+name), VersionIncompatible (core_version mismatch), KindUnknown (plugin kind not registered), RuntimeNotSupported (plugin declares no matching runtime).
For hook call errors use BroadcastErrors (partial broadcast failure) and DispatchMismatch (plugin returned wrong type) — both provide per-plugin breakdowns.
Do not instantiate plugins manually with new PluginClass() — always route through PluginRegistry so lifecycle, resources, and contract checks apply.
Do not store mutable state on plugin classes between hook calls — if state is needed, put it in a Resources-DI service with explicit lifecycle, otherwise contract tests will flag ambient state.
Plugin core_version in the manifest must match the installed dagstack-plugin-system major version — semver mismatches raise VersionIncompatible at discovery.

The cross-language contract is fixed in ADR-0001 (core architecture) and ADR-0002 (hook invocation semantics) of plugin-system-spec — all bindings (plugin-system-python, plugin-system-typescript) implement the same wire format and dispatch classes.

Error codes, taxonomies, and required error fields are fixed in ADR-0005 — bindings raise equivalent errors (ManifestInvalid, AmbiguousPlugin, VersionIncompatible, KindUnknown, RuntimeNotSupported, DependencyCycle, TeardownErrors) with same semantics.
